title: RACK1 maintains mouse hematopoietic stem cells by directly binding to and stabilizing LDB1
task: Elucidate RACK1's role in hematopoietic stem cell maintenance
key_results: Adult Rack1 deletion caused rapid HSC loss and hematopoietic failure; RACK1 stabilizes LDB1 protein by blocking ubiquitination-mediated degradation; prenatal Rack1 deletion reduced fetal liver HSCs
comments: The finding that RACK1 works through a single direct interaction (LDB1 stabilization) is mechanistically elegant, though additional RACK1 targets may contribute to HSC maintenance.

model_io.model: adult mouse hematopoietic system with inducible Rack1 deletion in IFN-I-responsive cells
fetal liver hematopoiesis with prenatal Rack1 deletion
inputs: constitutive Rack1 deletion in hematopoietic cells

model_io.model: biochemical interaction studies

hypotheses.hypothesis: RACK1 maintains HSC homeostasis by directly binding and stabilizing LDB1 protein
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; RACK1 prevents LDB1 ubiquitination and degradation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Rack1 deletion in IFN-I-responsive cells causes cell-intrinsic HSC defects and apoptosis
hypotheses.result: Supported by scRNA-seq showing aberrant transcriptional signatures and stressed HSC emergence

title: ATR is a critical dependency gene for uveal melanoma
task: Identify and validate ATR as a therapeutic target in uveal melanoma
key_results: ATR inhibition (VE-822) reduced colony and spheroid formation in three UM models; combination with paclitaxel produced significant synergy
comments: The finding that mitotic progression is critical for ATR-inhibited cell response suggests potential toxicity in normal dividing cells warrants consideration.

model_io.model: uveal melanoma cell lines (92.1, MEL270, MP38)
DepMap dependency analysis
outputs: ATR identified as key fitness regulator

hypotheses.hypothesis: Successful S phase completion and mitotic progression are critical determinants of UM response to ATR inhibition
hypotheses.result: Supported by RNA-seq pathway enrichment and synergy with microtubule inhibitors

title: Sitravatinib combined with osimertinib overcomes acquired osimertinib resistance in NSCLC by targeting AXL and the PI3K/AKT/GSK3β signaling pathway
task: Overcome acquired osimertinib resistance in EGFR-mutant NSCLC via combination therapy
key_results: Sitravatinib plus osimertinib showed markedly reinforced anti-tumor activity in vitro and in vivo compared to single agents; suppressed AXL and PI3K/AKT/GSK3β signaling
comments: The mechanism of AXL activation driving osimertinib resistance is well-established, making this a rational but incremental combination strategy.

model_io.model: NSCLC cell lines with acquired osimertinib resistance
nude mouse xenograft

hypotheses.hypothesis: Sitravatinib overcomes osimertinib resistance by inhibiting AXL and downstream PI3K/AKT/GSK3β signaling while reversing EMT
hypotheses.result: Confirmed through Western blot and functional assays

title: Multimodal radiomic and foundation-model MRI features converge on basal ganglia patterns in Parkinson’s motor subtypes
task: Discriminating Parkinson's motor subtypes using multimodal MRI representations
key_results: Radiomic features outperformed foundation-model embeddings (AUC 0.664 vs 0.592); combined FLAIR+SWI radiomics with clinical scores achieved AUC 0.79 ± 0.10
comments: Basal ganglia SWI-derived features drive discrimination, but modest performance gains and small sample size limit immediate clinical translation.

model_io.model: Radiomic feature extraction and BrainIAC transformer foundation model; nested stratified five-fold cross-validation with multiple ML classifiers
outputs: saliency maps highlighting basal ganglia regions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multimodal MRI-derived features can discriminate TD and PIGD motor subtypes better than clinical scores alone
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed; combined radiomics+clinical scores achieved AUC 0.79, superior to either modality alone

hypotheses.hypothesis: Foundation-model embeddings match or exceed conventional radiomics for PD subtype discrimination
hypotheses.result: Rejected; radiomics consistently outperformed embeddings

title: Development and comparison of machine learning-based clinical diagnostic models for girls with suspected central precocious puberty
task: Machine learning pre-screening for central precocious puberty diagnosis
key_results: CatBoost achieved AUROC 0.894 ± 0.024 with 84% sensitivity and 94.8% NPV; could avoid 63 unnecessary GnRH tests per 100 cases
comments: Strong clinical utility demonstrated, but external validation on independent cohorts would strengthen claims for adoption as pre-screening tool.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Machine learning models using routine clinical data can pre-screen for CPP with sufficient accuracy to reduce invasive testing

title: Immunoinformatics-guided in silico design of a multi-epitope peptide vaccine against Mycobacterium tuberculosis
task: Immunoinformatics-driven multi-epitope peptide vaccine design against Mycobacterium tuberculosis
key_results: Final 429 amino acid construct (43.947 kDa) with predicted stability index 23.25, docked strongly to TLR4 (−1175.2 kcal/mol) and TLR2 (−1022.8 kcal/mol); immune simulation showed strong immunogenic profile
comments: Comprehensive in silico design pipeline is methodologically sound, but entirely computational predictions require mandatory in vitro and in vivo experimental validation before clinical consideration.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Selected conserved Mtb proteins contain immunogenic epitopes suitable for multi-epitope vaccine design
hypotheses.result: Supported; 5 B-cell, 4 HTL, and 9 CTL epitopes identified and integrated

hypotheses.hypothesis: Designed construct binds strongly to TLRs and generates robust in silico immune response
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; strong TLR docking affinities and stable MD interactions; immune simulation predicted immunogenicity

title: Comprehensive analysis of the prognosis of gastric cancer on the basis of three disulfidptosis-related lncRNA signatures
task: Prognostic modeling of gastric cancer using disulfidptosis-related lncRNA signatures
key_results: Three independent signatures developed with C-index > 0.6 and time-dependent AUC > 0.6 at 1, 3, 5 years; Signature 3 showed marginally superior C-index; 7 drugs identified with predicted differential sensitivity
comments: Multi-screening strategy with train-test splitting reduces overfitting risk, but purely computational predictions lack validation; external cohort confirmation is essential before clinical adoption.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Focal adhesion and ECM-receptor interaction pathways are implicated in disulfidptosis-related GC mechanisms
